source.title: Single-neuron mechanisms underlying cost-benefit analysis in frontal cortex

confidence_rationale: High source quality (primate single-unit, top venue) but only moderate mapping fidelity: it measures neural representation of decision variables, not separate LEARNABILITY of channels nor any action-conversion benefit. Net supports the no-single-scalar premise while documenting a shared/categorical bottleneck.
failure_signatures: The integrated subjective-value population was relatively few in number; most frontal neurons instead encoded categorical decision-type (delay- vs effort-based), so a learner exposed to finer channels might discover category gating rather than value-channel mixing.
Specialization was incomplete (ACC carried both cost types), so the putative channels are not cleanly orthogonal.

mapping.source_claim_statement: OFC, ACC, DLPFC and cingulate motor area neurons largely encode the TYPE of cost-benefit decision (delay vs effort) with partial area specialization; only a minority (mainly ACC) carry an integrated subjective-value signal, challenging the idea that OFC computes an abstract scalar value.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-451's premise that frontal control is NOT a single compressed value scalar -- cost dimensions are carried in partially segregated populations, so exposing several finer separately-learnable channels has a biological substrate.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Primate single-unit recording of decision-variable REPRESENTATION; it does not measure whether channels are separately LEARNABLE by a gating layer, nor whether finer granularity improves conversion of non-motor influence into committed action. Segregation is necessary-but-not-sufficient for the claim.
mapping.source_context: Macaque single-neuron recording during delay-based and effort-based cost-benefit choice.

confidence_components.notes: Most load-bearing single datum: documents both segregation AND a shared/categorical comparator bottleneck, i.e. evidence the conversion ceiling architecture exists.
